A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OKGQA/OKGQA-P study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison. Reporting inconsistencies in v3 do not constitute missing source material.

before.justification: V2 reports original LLM benchmark results, KG perturbation experiments and human/LLM query-quality agreement measurements in Table 2, Figures 4–6 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark results and adds IRCoT comparisons, multilingual-context results, evaluator validation and query–DBpedia alignment measurements.

M1.justification: The prize-cost triplet/path/PCST retrieval procedures, PPR pruning, KG-guided generation and four perturbation operators remain unchanged. Reorganized explanations and multilingual testing do not establish a new algorithm, objective or method component.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds evaluation with multilingual DBpedia entities and relations in Greek, Polish, Portuguese, Spanish and English, substantially extending KG input-language coverage beyond the original monolingual setting. This concerns knowledge context, not demonstrated multilingual questions. The benchmarks listed in Table 7 are descriptive comparisons, not additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Wikipedia-document IRCoT baselines using GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, introducing an external-text retrieval comparison absent from v2's experiments. It also removes standalone CoT rows for Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-9B while retaining their CoT+SC rows.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a 100-question validation using three LLM evaluators and three human annotators rating anonymized responses on a 1–5 scale, plus a 300-query multilingual comparison. Figure 2 and Table 7 report expansion from 850 to 2,050 questions without clarifying which results use the expanded set. Appendix B.2's new 3–4-hop statistic conflicts with the retained two-hop construction description; an actual retrieval-setting change or rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's query-quality agreement and KG perturbation analyses, v3 adds answer-evaluator validation against humans and alternative LLM judges in Appendix A.4. Appendix B also adds multilingual-context comparison and measurements of query–DBpedia entity coverage, relation connectivity and subgraph alignment.

E5.justification: Both versions report performance with ± values and use Pearson correlation and Cohen's kappa. V3 applies these existing statistical practices to additional evaluator comparisons, without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or an explanation of the ± terms.

E6.justification: All 33 shared Table 2 rows retain identical values; two IRCoT rows are added and three standalone CoT rows removed. New IRCoT FActScores are 69.45% for GPT-4o and 65.72% for GPT-4o-mini. Additional results include multilingual FActScore of 72.83%, evaluator kappa values of 0.70–0.84, human–G-Eval correlation of 0.78, and DBpedia alignment statistics. These are newly reported comparisons and analyses, not improved scores for retained experiments.

T1.justification: The likelihood factorization and approximation, prize-cost objectives, PPR recurrence and ATS/SC2D/SD2 definitions are mathematically unchanged. V3 separates v2's Equation 1 into two numbered equations and abbreviates some notation, without adding or revising theoretical assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and central claims about KG retrieval reducing hallucinations, limitations of internal reasoning alone, and robustness to partial KG contamination. The rewritten introduction preserves these claims; the broader subgraph-performance finding remains in Section 4.2.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations concerning evaluator independence, dataset grounding, multilingual knowledge diversity and duplication, and IRCoT's vulnerability to irrelevant context. Its blanket KG-superiority interpretation overstates Table 2: GPT-4o triplet correctness is 65.37%, below IRCoT's 66.33%. The original domain-specific and static-KG limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 first identifies GPT-4o-mini as the evaluation backbone and supplies November 2024–January 2025 model-use windows. It documents sampling, annotators, rating scales and multilingual construction for the added studies. These disclosures do not establish a change of evaluator for retained experiments. Existing prompts, PPR parameters and the code/data link destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Balas (1989) and the Gu/Li (2024) LLM-judge surveys, removes several motivation references, and adds Table 7's benchmark comparison. The related-work discussion is largely retained. IRCoT was already cited in v2; its new experimental participation is distinct from a new cited work.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the introduction and framework exposition, separates formalization into Section 3.1, and converts perturbation and retrieval descriptions into lists. It integrates earlier open-ended-question motivation into the introduction and reorganizes Appendix A into clearer subsections, with related work and prompts moving to Appendices C and D.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 5–7, changes Table 2's row grouping, moves table captions below the tables and relocates several retained displays. The existing eight figures remain, with unchanged plot images, and the overall two-column visual design is preserved.

improvement.justification: The new Wikipedia-RAG comparison and answer-level human/cross-model validation address evidential gaps in v2, improving support for KG benefits and evaluation validity. However, the unexplained 850-to-2,050 expansion, conflicting hop descriptions, and overbroad IRCoT correctness claim limit the gain. The multilingual comparison also reuses Table 2's monolingual values without clearly reconciling them with its 300-query sample. The net improvement is therefore limited.
